concepts.name: Fourth Buddhist Council under Kanishka
key_dimensions: Venue: Kashmir (Kundalvana) vs. Jalandhar — competing traditions and UPSC trap on location
Chairperson: Vasumitra presided, Ashvaghosha as vice-chair — roles often confused
Outcome: Compilation of Mahavibhasha (encyclopedia of Abhidharma) — distinguishing it from earlier councils' outputs
Contrast with previous three councils: patronage, language (Sanskrit vs. Pali), and sectarian context

concepts.name: Kanishka's Role in the Mahayana–Hinayana Schism
key_dimensions: Fourth Council as the formal crystallization point of Mahayana school
Kanishka's personal affiliation: Mahayana patronage vs. earlier Kushan religious eclecticism
Hinayana (Theravada) rejection of Fourth Council's authority — sectarian fault lines
UPSC trap: associating all Buddhist councils with Theravada; Kanishka's council is specifically Mahayana-linked

concepts.name: Ashvaghosha: Scholar-Poet at Kanishka's Court
key_dimensions: Key works: Buddhacharita (biography of Buddha in Sanskrit), Saundarananda, Sariputraprakarana
Significance of Buddhacharita as first systematic Sanskrit Buddhist biography — literary history angle
Ashvaghosha as a convert from Brahminism — ideological symbolism for Kanishka's patronage
Role in Fourth Council vs. his literary contributions — two distinct dimensions often conflated

concepts.name: Vasumitra and Mahavibhasha
key_dimensions: Mahavibhasha: nature, content, and its role as the doctrinal foundation of Sarvastivada school
Vasumitra as president of Fourth Council — distinction from his philosophical works
Sarvastivada school's geographical dominance in Northwest India under Kushan patronage
UPSC trap: confusing Vasumitra (Kushan-era) with another Vasumitra mentioned in other contexts

concepts.name: Kanishka's Era and Chronological Controversy
key_dimensions: Kanishka Era (78 CE theory): link to Saka era — contested but widely cited
Alternative dating (127 CE): implications for synchronizing Kushan history with Roman and Chinese records
Why exact dating matters for UPSC: questions on 'first century CE' vs 'second century CE' classification
Rabatak inscription's role in revising Kushan chronology — recent epigraphic evidence

concepts.name: Kanishka's Coinage and Religious Syncretism
key_dimensions: Coins depicting Buddha ('Boddo') — earliest numismatic representation of Buddha in human form
Multi-religious pantheon on coins: Greek (Helios), Iranian (Mithra, Ahura Mazda), and Indian deities
Buddha represented alongside Zoroastrian and Greek gods — evidence of eclectic patronage, not exclusive Buddhism
UPSC trap: overemphasizing Kanishka as purely Buddhist based on Buddhist patronage, ignoring coin evidence of syncretism

concepts.name: Kanishka's Stupa at Peshawar (Kanishka Stupa)
key_dimensions: Location: Purushapura (modern Peshawar) — capital of Kushan Empire
Description by Chinese pilgrims Fa-Hien and Xuan Zang: one of the tallest structures of the ancient world
Kanishka relic casket (Peshawar casket): inscription, iconography, and its Buddhist relic context
Archaeological rediscovery in 1908–1909 — connecting textual and material evidence

concepts.name: Kanishka Casket (Peshawar Relic Casket): Inscription and Art
key_dimensions: Inscription in Kharosthi script mentioning 'Kanishka' — primary epigraphic evidence of his name
Iconography: Buddha flanked by Brahma and Indra, Kanishka figure at base
Material: bronze — craftsmanship reflecting Gandhara artistic tradition
UPSC angle: distinguishing this from other Kushan inscriptions; its role as direct evidence of his Buddhist identity

concepts.name: Gandhara Art: Kanishka's Patronage and Greco-Buddhist Synthesis
key_dimensions: Gandhara school's defining features: Hellenistic influence, use of schist stone, realistic Buddha depiction
Kanishka's role as the greatest patron of Gandhara art — institutional patronage vs. Mathura school
Gandhara vs. Mathura school: stylistic, geographical, and patronage differences — classic UPSC comparison
First anthropomorphic representation of Buddha: both schools claim it — UPSC trap on priority

concepts.name: Mathura School of Art under Kushan Period
key_dimensions: Indigenous tradition vs. Gandhara's Hellenistic influence — material (red sandstone) and stylistic contrast
Kanishka's headless statue at Mathura — epigraphic evidence of his name and title 'Maharaja Rajatiraja'
Mathura as a Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu art center simultaneously — eclecticism under Kushan rule
UPSC trap: assuming Gandhara = Kushan patronage exclusively; Mathura equally important under Kushans

concepts.name: Nagarjuna and Madhyamaka Philosophy under Kushan Influence
key_dimensions: Nagarjuna's Madhyamaka (Shunyata doctrine): philosophical foundation of Mahayana Buddhism
Temporal association with Kanishka's era — though exact contemporaneity is debated
Nagarjuna's Mulamadhyamakakarika as the key text — distinguishing his philosophical from institutional role
UPSC trap: placing Nagarjuna exclusively at Kanishka's court (association is indirect, not definitively confirmed)

concepts.name: Spread of Buddhism to Central Asia and China under Kanishka
key_dimensions: Silk Route control by Kushans: geographical enabler of Buddhist missionary activity
Transmission of Mahayana Buddhism to China: Kanishka's era as the turning point
Role of monks like Lokaksema in translating Buddhist texts into Chinese
Kanishka's empire as the 'bridge' between Indian Buddhism and East Asian Buddhism — a geopolitical-religious nexus

concepts.name: Kanishka's Titles and Political-Religious Authority
key_dimensions: Title 'Devaputra' (Son of God): borrowed from Chinese 'Son of Heaven' — cross-cultural legitimacy claim
Rabatak inscription titles: 'Maharaja, Rajatiraja, Devaputra, Kaisara' — multi-civilizational claims
Comparison with Ashoka's use of Dhamma for political legitimacy — Buddhism as statecraft tool
UPSC trap: 'Devaputra' title — distinguishing its origin and use across Kushans vs. Guptas

concepts.name: Charaka and Sushruta: Medical Scholarship under Kanishka's Patronage
key_dimensions: Charaka Samhita's redaction attributed to Charaka at Kanishka's court — Ayurvedic text preservation
Distinction between original Agnivesha text and Charaka's revision — layered authorship problem
UPSC trap: placing Charaka firmly as a 'court physician' of Kanishka vs. the contested nature of this claim
Relationship between Buddhist monasteries and medical knowledge transmission in this period

concepts.name: Buddhist Missionary Activity and Monastic Institutions under Kanishka
key_dimensions: Construction of viharas and stupas across Gandhara, Kashmir, and Central Asia — institutional patronage
Role of Buddhist monasteries as centers of learning, trade, and diplomacy along Silk Routes
Kanishka vs. Ashoka: comparative patronage models — edicts vs. councils vs. construction
UPSC trap: attributing all Buddhist monastic expansion in NW India to Ashoka, ignoring Kanishka's equally significant role

concepts.name: Rabatak Inscription: Epigraphic Evidence for Kanishka
key_dimensions: Discovery: 1993, Rabatak (Afghanistan) — relatively recent find with major historical implications
Content: Kanishka's genealogy, his accession, cities under his rule, and religious dedications to Iranian gods
Language: Bactrian (Greek script) — significance for understanding Kushan court language
UPSC relevance: challenges earlier assumptions about Kanishka's chronology and religious identity; tests awareness of recent archaeological findings

concepts.name: Kanishka and the Bodhisattva Concept in Mahayana
key_dimensions: Mahayana's Bodhisattva ideal vs. Hinayana's Arhat ideal — doctrinal difference patronized by Kanishka
Artistic representation of Bodhisattvas (especially Maitreya and Avalokitesvara) in Gandhara art
Kanishka's patronage as institutionalizing the devotional (bhakti-like) dimension of Buddhism
UPSC trap: associating Bodhisattva concept only with later Gupta period art, ignoring its Kushan-era visual consolidation

concepts.name: Chinese Pilgrim Accounts as Sources for Kanishka's Buddhist Legacy
key_dimensions: Fa-Hien (399–414 CE) and Xuan Zang (629–645 CE): descriptions of Kanishka's stupa and Buddhist sites
Time gap between Kanishka's reign and pilgrim visits — methodological limitation of using pilgrim accounts
What pilgrims corroborate vs. what they embellish — critical source analysis for UPSC
UPSC trap: treating pilgrim accounts as contemporary sources; they are retrospective and hagiographic

concepts.name: Comparison: Ashoka vs. Kanishka as Buddhist Patrons
key_dimensions: Method of patronage: Ashoka — edicts, dhamma, non-violence policy; Kanishka — councils, art, missionary expansion
Sectarian alignment: Ashoka — Theravada (debated); Kanishka — Mahayana (more definitively)
Geographical spread: Ashoka — subcontinent + Sri Lanka; Kanishka — Central Asia + China
UPSC trap: assuming Ashoka's patronage was more impactful; Kanishka's role in globalizing Buddhism is equally transformative
